title: Familiar world-events and conspiracy-related answer-bank expansion
scope: Finite authored expansion; exact propositions are graded rather than entire subjects or every associated theory.
licensing: Original concise statements and explanations. Institutional sources are linked for verification; their prose and media are not republished. No blanket license claimed for linked sites.

source_review.method: Browsed institutional primary histories, archives, scientific-agency explanations, treaty records and the relevant organizations' own founding histories. Dates and classification apply only to each displayed proposition.
source_review.limits: Familiarity is editorial, not measured rarity. True founding/testing facts about Illuminati, Freemasonry, Bilderberg and Area 51 do not validate world-control or extraterrestrial claims. An unidentified UAP is not proof of aliens. Military conflicts are scoped by the stated theater or diplomatic milestone rather than one disputed universal start date. Sources do not imply approval of the institutions described. No unresolved extraterrestrial-identification question is graded as resolved.

subjects.name: World War I
subjects.statement: World War I was fought from 1914 to 1918.
subjects.explanation: The conflict involved the Allied and Central Powers; later peace settlements were separate from the 1918 armistice.

subjects.name: World War II
subjects.statement: Germany invaded Poland in September 1939, starting World War II in Europe.
subjects.explanation: The European war began in 1939; fighting in Asia had already begun earlier.

subjects.name: Korean War
subjects.statement: The Korean War began in 1950 and fighting was halted by an armistice in 1953.
subjects.explanation: The armistice stopped the fighting without becoming a comprehensive peace treaty.

subjects.name: Vietnam War
subjects.statement: The United States signed the Paris peace agreement concerning Vietnam in January 1973.
subjects.explanation: The agreement and US withdrawal did not mean that all fighting in Vietnam ended that year.
subjects.publisher: US Department of State, Office of the Historian

subjects.name: Gulf War
subjects.statement: A US-led coalition fought Iraqi forces in 1991 after Iraq invaded Kuwait.
subjects.explanation: The 1990 invasion and 1991 coalition campaign are distinct stages of the crisis.
subjects.publisher: US Department of State, Office of the Historian

subjects.name: American Revolution
subjects.statement: The American Revolutionary War was fought from 1775 to 1783.
subjects.explanation: The conflict began between Britain and its North American colonies and developed into a wider international war.

subjects.name: American Civil War
subjects.statement: The American Civil War was fought from 1861 to 1865.
subjects.explanation: The National Park Service preserves battlefields and records the conflict between the Union and Confederacy.

subjects.name: French Revolution
subjects.statement: The storming of the Bastille took place in Paris in July 1789 during the French Revolution.
subjects.explanation: The event became a defining symbol of the revolution; it was not the whole revolution in a single day.

subjects.name: Great Depression
subjects.statement: The United States experienced a severe economic depression during the 1930s.
subjects.explanation: Federal Reserve historians distinguish the long depression from the October 1929 stock-market crash.

subjects.name: Wall Street Crash of 1929
subjects.statement: US share prices collapsed in the stock-market crash of October 1929.
subjects.explanation: The crash was followed by a much longer depression; it was not the only cause.

subjects.name: 2008 financial crisis
subjects.statement: The United States experienced a recession from December 2007 to June 2009 during the global financial crisis.
subjects.explanation: Housing and financial-market distress were central to the crisis; the dates refer to the US recession.

subjects.name: Collapse of the Soviet Union
subjects.statement: The Soviet Union dissolved in 1991.
subjects.explanation: The failed August coup and the emergence of independent republics were part of the breakup.
subjects.publisher: US Department of State, Office of the Historian

subjects.name: Brexit
subjects.statement: A majority of voters in the UK referendum of June 2016 voted to leave the European Union.
subjects.explanation: The referendum was followed by negotiations and formal UK withdrawal in January 2020.

subjects.name: 1994 genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda
subjects.statement: A genocide against the Tutsi took place in Rwanda in 1994.
subjects.explanation: The UN records the atrocity and subsequent prosecutions; the proposition avoids disputed exact totals.

subjects.name: Holocaust
subjects.statement: Nazi Germany and its collaborators systematically murdered six million Jews during the Holocaust.
subjects.explanation: The museum documents this genocide and the persecution and killing of other groups.

subjects.name: Trinity nuclear test
subjects.statement: The first nuclear test took place in New Mexico on July 16, 1945.
subjects.explanation: The plutonium device was developed as part of the Manhattan Project.

subjects.name: Atomic bombing of Hiroshima
subjects.statement: The United States dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima on August 6, 1945.
subjects.explanation: The NPS timeline records the mission without claiming that one event alone ended the war.

subjects.name: Atomic bombing of Nagasaki
subjects.statement: The United States dropped an atomic bomb on Nagasaki on August 9, 1945.
subjects.explanation: This was a separate bombing three days after Hiroshima.

subjects.name: Manhattan Project
subjects.statement: The Manhattan Project developed the first atomic weapons during World War II.
subjects.explanation: Its sites included Los Alamos, Oak Ridge and Hanford; it was a real wartime program.

subjects.name: Smallpox eradication
subjects.statement: WHO declared smallpox eradicated in 1980.
subjects.explanation: The declaration followed an international campaign; it did not mean every infectious disease had disappeared.

subjects.name: COVID-19 pandemic
subjects.statement: WHO characterized the COVID-19 outbreak as a pandemic on March 11, 2020.
subjects.explanation: This date describes WHO's assessment of worldwide spread, not the date the virus first existed.

subjects.name: 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami
subjects.statement: An earthquake off Sumatra generated the Indian Ocean tsunami on December 26, 2004.
subjects.explanation: The waves devastated coasts around the Indian Ocean; no single final casualty total is used.
subjects.publisher: US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration

subjects.name: 2010 Haiti earthquake
subjects.statement: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Haiti on January 12, 2010.
subjects.explanation: The USGS reconnaissance report records extensive damage; exact death estimates are not used to grade this statement.

subjects.name: 2011 Tohoku earthquake and tsunami
subjects.statement: A powerful offshore earthquake struck northeastern Japan on March 11, 2011 and generated a tsunami.
subjects.explanation: The earthquake and tsunami are distinct from the associated Fukushima nuclear accident.

subjects.name: Hurricane Katrina
subjects.statement: Hurricane Katrina struck the northern US Gulf Coast in August 2005.
subjects.explanation: The National Weather Service documents the storm, landfalls and destructive surge.

subjects.name: Suez Crisis
subjects.statement: Egypt nationalized the Suez Canal Company in 1956, triggering an international crisis.
subjects.explanation: The crisis involved Egypt, Britain, France, Israel and major-power diplomacy.
subjects.publisher: US Department of State, Office of the Historian

subjects.name: Opening of the Panama Canal
subjects.statement: The Panama Canal opened in 1914.
subjects.explanation: The canal provided a shipping route across the isthmus between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
subjects.publisher: US Department of State, Office of the Historian

subjects.name: Indian independence
subjects.statement: India became independent from British rule in August 1947.
subjects.explanation: Independence accompanied partition; the transition was not free of violence.
subjects.publisher: US Department of State, Office of the Historian

subjects.name: End of apartheid
subjects.statement: The dismantling of apartheid led to a democratic government in South Africa in 1994.
subjects.explanation: The transition occurred through a series of steps in the early 1990s rather than one overnight change.
subjects.publisher: US Department of State, Office of the Historian

subjects.name: Assassination of John F. Kennedy
subjects.statement: President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas on November 22, 1963.
subjects.explanation: The event is documented. This statement does not decide competing claims about additional conspirators.

subjects.name: Tiananmen Square crackdown
subjects.statement: Chinese authorities violently suppressed the Beijing demonstrations in June 1989.
subjects.explanation: The historical account records the crackdown; no disputed precise casualty count is used.
subjects.publisher: US Department of State, Office of the Historian

subjects.name: Wright brothers first flight
subjects.statement: The Wright brothers made powered flights in North Carolina on December 17, 1903.
subjects.explanation: The Smithsonian records the 1903 Flyer and the short flights that launched the aerial age.
subjects.publisher: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum

subjects.name: Boston Tea Party
subjects.statement: Protesters dumped tea into Boston Harbor on December 16, 1773.
subjects.explanation: The National Park Service timeline documents the protest against British policies.

subjects.name: March on Washington
aliases: March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom
subjects.statement: The March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom took place on August 28, 1963.
subjects.explanation: The demonstration brought a large crowd to Washington, DC to demand civil and economic rights.

subjects.name: 1980 Mount St. Helens eruption
subjects.statement: Mount St. Helens erupted catastrophically on May 18, 1980.
subjects.explanation: A collapsing flank, lateral blast and ash eruption were part of the documented sequence.

subjects.name: Exxon Valdez oil spill
subjects.statement: The tanker Exxon Valdez ran aground in Alaska on March 24, 1989 and spilled oil.
subjects.explanation: NOAA records the grounding at Bligh Reef in Prince William Sound.
subjects.publisher: US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration

subjects.name: Three Mile Island accident
subjects.statement: Three Mile Island Unit 2 partially melted down in Pennsylvania in March 1979.
subjects.explanation: The NRC describes the accident and changes to regulation, training and emergency planning.

subjects.name: Paris Agreement
subjects.statement: The Paris Agreement on climate change was adopted in December 2015.
subjects.explanation: Adoption in 2015 and entry into force in 2016 were separate legal steps.
subjects.publisher: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change

subjects.name: Montreal Protocol
subjects.statement: The Montreal Protocol on ozone-depleting substances was adopted in September 1987.
subjects.explanation: It regulates substances that damage the ozone layer; it is a different treaty from the Paris climate agreement.

subjects.name: Area 51
subjects.statement: Area 51 was used to test the CIA's U-2 reconnaissance aircraft in the 1950s.
subjects.explanation: The aircraft-testing role does not establish claims about captured extraterrestrial craft.

subjects.name: Bavarian Illuminati
subjects.statement: Adam Weishaupt founded the society later known as the Illuminati in Ingolstadt in 1776.
subjects.explanation: The historical society existed. Its founding is not evidence that a hidden group controls modern world events.

subjects.name: Freemasonry
subjects.statement: Four London lodges formed a Grand Lodge in 1717.
subjects.explanation: The United Grand Lodge of England records this history; the statement does not endorse world-control allegations.

subjects.name: Bilderberg Meeting
subjects.statement: The first Bilderberg Meeting took place in the Netherlands in 1954.
subjects.explanation: The organizer records the meeting. Private discussions alone do not establish a secret world-government claim.

subjects.name: 9/11 controlled-demolition claim
subjects.statement: The Twin Towers were brought down by secretly planted demolition explosives on September 11, 2001.
subjects.explanation: NIST found no corroborating evidence for that hypothesis and documented an impact-and-fire collapse sequence.
subjects.publisher: US National Institute of Standards and Technology

subjects.name: WTC 7 demolition claim
subjects.statement: World Trade Center 7 was brought down by a concealed demolition blast.
subjects.explanation: NIST investigated the blast hypothesis, found no supporting blast evidence and described fire-induced structural failure.
subjects.publisher: US National Institute of Standards and Technology

subjects.name: MMR-autism claim
subjects.statement: The MMR vaccine causes autism.
subjects.explanation: Large, high-quality studies and WHO safety reviews do not support a causal link between vaccines and autism.

subjects.name: Protocols authenticity claim
aliases: Protocols of the Elders of Zion
subjects.statement: The Protocols of the Elders of Zion are an authentic record of a Jewish plan to control the world.
subjects.explanation: The museum traces this antisemitic text's fabrication and plagiarism. It is a forgery, not evidence against Jewish people.

subjects.name: Great Wall visible-from-Moon myth
subjects.statement: The Great Wall of China is visible to the unaided eye from the Moon.
subjects.explanation: NASA identifies this as a myth; magnified photographs from low Earth orbit are a different question.

subjects.name: Pentagon alien-confirmation claim
subjects.statement: The Pentagon's 2024 historical UAP review confirmed that alien spacecraft had visited Earth.
subjects.explanation: AARO found no evidence that reviewed sightings had been confirmed as extraterrestrial technology. An unidentified sighting is not itself an alien identification.
subjects.publisher: US Department of Defense, All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office
